lessons.title: Greetings
lessons.goal: Say hello, goodbye, thank you and sorry.

lessons.title: Who are you?
lessons.goal: Say your name, nationality and job with 是 and 叫.

lessons.title: How are you?
lessons.goal: Ask yes / no questions with 吗 and bounce them back with 呢.

lessons.title: When you don't understand
lessons.goal: Ask to repeat, slow down, explain or write it down.

lessons.title: This and that
lessons.goal: Point at things and people; say whose they are with 的.

lessons.title: My family
lessons.goal: Talk about family members with 有 / 没有 and count them.

lessons.title: Age and jobs
lessons.goal: Ask and give age and job; say where you work with 在.

lessons.title: Describing people
lessons.goal: Describe people with 很, 太……了, 真 and 不太.

items.note: 3rd + 3rd tone: the first 3rd tone is spoken as a 2nd: ní hǎo.
您 is the polite "you": for older people, teachers and customers.
们 makes a plural of people: 你们 = you (plural).
Title after the name or alone: 王老师好！
The second 谢 is in the neutral tone: short and light.
不 is bù, but bú before a 4th tone (客 kè).
The usual answer to 对不起.
是 links two nouns: A 是 B = A is B.
不是 bú shì: 不 rises before the 4th tone of 是.
他 (he) and 她 (she) sound the same: tā.

items.ruby: 你[nǐ]叫[jiào]什么[shén me]名字[míng zi]？

items.note: Put your own name after 叫.
A polite question; answer with 我姓 + surname.
Country + 人 = a person from there.

items.ruby: 认识[rèn shi]你[nǐ]很[hěn]高兴[gāo xìng]。
items.note: 很 before an adjective is often just a link, not "very".
Three 3rd tones in a row: usually spoken wó yé hěn.
Correct but a little formal; friends say 最近怎么样？
Three 3rd tones: usually spoken wó hén hǎo.
呢 bounces the question back: "and you?"
也 (also) goes before the verb or adjective, never at the end.
3rd + 3rd tone: the first 3rd tone is spoken as a 2nd: ké yǐ.
不太 bú tài = not very.

items.ruby: 最近[zuì jìn]怎么样[zěn me yàng]？

items.note: 挺……的 = quite. 3rd + 3rd tone: the first 3rd tone is spoken as a 2nd: tíng hǎo.

items.ruby: 你[nǐ]是[shì]中国人[Zhōng guó rén]吗[ma]？
items.note: Add 吗 to any statement to make a yes / no question.

items.ruby: 不[bù]，我[wǒ]是[shì]英国人[Yīng guó rén]。

items.note: Chinese has no single word for "yes": repeat the verb (是 / 有 / 会) or say 对.
Verb + 不 + result: 听不懂 = listen but not understand. 不 here is neutral.
一 is yī, but yí before a 4th tone (遍 biàn).

items.ruby: 请[qǐng]说[shuō]慢[màn]一点儿[yì diǎn r]。
items.note: 一点儿 yìdiǎnr: 一 is yì before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone. The 儿 ending is northern; in the south people say 一点.

items.en: How do you say this in Chinese?
items.ruby: 这个[zhè ge]用[yòng]中文[Zhōng wén]怎么[zěn me]说[shuō]？
这[zhè]是[shì]什么[shén me]意思[yì si]？

items.en: I can speak a little Chinese.
items.ruby: 我[wǒ]会[huì]说[shuō]一点儿[yì diǎn r]中文[Zhōng wén]。
items.note: 会 = can, a skill you have learned.
Answer with the verb of the question: 会 / 不会.
Verb + 一下 (yíxià) softens a request: "just ... a bit".

items.en: Excuse me, are you Teacher Wang?
items.ruby: 请问[qǐng wèn]，你[nǐ]是[shì]王[Wáng]老师[lǎo shī]吗[ma]？
items.kana: qingwen ni shi wang laoshi ma
items.romaji: Qǐngwèn, nǐ shì Wáng lǎoshī ma?
items.note: 请问 = "may I ask": the polite way to start a question to a stranger.
的 links owner and thing: 我的书 = my book.
谁 is shéi in everyday speech (shuí when read carefully).
With close people 的 is usually dropped: 我朋友, 我妈妈.
我的 alone = mine.

items.kana: zhe shi ni de shouji ma
items.romaji: Zhè shì nǐ de shǒujī ma?

items.note: 这 zhè = this (near), 那 nà = that (far).

items.en: How many people are there in your family?
items.kana: ni jia you ji kou ren
items.romaji: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
items.note: 口 (mouth) is the measure word for family members.

items.en: There are four of us in my family.
items.kana: wo jia you si kou ren
items.romaji: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.

items.en: Dad, Mum, my younger sister and me.
items.ruby: 爸爸[bà ba]、妈妈[mā ma]、妹妹[mèi mei]和[hé]我[wǒ]。
items.note: Kinship words double the syllable; the second one is neutral.

items.en: Do you have brothers or sisters?
items.ruby: 你[nǐ]有[yǒu]兄弟姐妹[xiōng dì jiě mèi]吗[ma]？

items.note: 一个 yí ge: 个 was originally gè (4th), so 一 rises.
有 is negated with 没, never with 不.
Written nǚ'ér: an apostrophe goes before a syllable that starts with a, o or e.
两 (not 二) before a measure word.

items.en: How old are you? (to an adult)
items.note: To a child: 你几岁了？ To an older person: 您多大年纪了？
No 是 before an age.

items.en: How old are you? (to a child)

items.ruby: 你[nǐ]做[zuò]什么[shén me]工作[gōng zuò]？
我[wǒ]在[zài]公司[gōng sī]工作[gōng zuò]。
items.note: The place (在 + place) comes before the verb.

items.ruby: 她[tā]在[zài]医院[yī yuàn]工作[gōng zuò]。
你[nǐ]在[zài]哪儿[nǎ r]工作[gōng zuò]？
items.note: 哪儿 nǎr (north) = 哪里 nǎli (south).
Adjectives need no 是: 他很高, never 他是高.
3rd + 3rd tone: the first 3rd tone is spoken as a 2nd: hén hǎo.

items.en: Your little sister is very cute.
items.ruby: 你[nǐ]妹妹[mèi mei]很[hěn]可爱[kě ài]。

items.note: 太 + adjective + 了 = "so ...!" (or "too ...").
Literally "her friends are many".
多 + adjective = how ... ?
一米八 = 1.80 m; the unit for the second part is left out.
